documents.title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBen

documents.title: Integrative multi-omic mapping of urinary and intrarenal immune landscapes in lupus nephritis identifies convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs.
documents.abstract: Renal biopsy is the gold standard for classifying lupus nephritis (LN), but due to its invasiveness and difficult longitudinal follow-up, it incompletely captures immune and histopathological dynamics. Urinary single-cell transcriptomic analysis has been proposed as a minimally invasive approach for monitoring LN, while renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provide high-resolution reference maps of the intrarenal environment. We performed a systematic scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to evaluate direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance and pathway molecular converg

documents.title: CD44+ Proximal Tubular Epithelial Cells May Be Involved in Renal Fibrosis and Inflammation via TGF-β Signaling in Hyperuricemic Nephropathy.
documents.abstract: The prevalence of hyperuricemia (HUA) is continuously increasing and HUA may eventually develop into irreversible hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN). Injured proximal tubule (PT) in the HUA microenvironment plays an important role in the progression of HN. However, the underlying pathological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between HUA kidneys and control groups were screened from bulk RNA sequencing data to identify abnormally activated signaling. Subsequently, PT cell-subtypes related to injury and repair were identified in single-cell RNA sequenc
documents.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling

documents.title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data u

documents.title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues.
documents.abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of

documents.title: GLAND: Resolving small and non-continuous tissue domains via a hybrid attention mechanism.
documents.abstract: Recent advances in spatial transcriptomic technology provide unprecedented insights into tissue architecture by enabling high-throughput gene expression profiling with the corresponding spatial context. While identifying spatial domains is a prerequisite for understanding tissue heterogeneity and functional organization, current computational methods often fail to resolve non-continuous or small domains that, despite their biological significance, exhibit complex spatial distribution.

documents.title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates.
documents.abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this li
documents.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling

documents.title: Integrated transcriptomics reveal fibroblast-monocyte crosstalk with JAK-STAT activation associated with Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the spatial and molecular mechanisms of Parvimonas micra-induced periodontitis, which remains poorly understood. We used bulk RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to investigate gingival responses in ligature and P. micra-induced rat periodontitis model and validated the findings in human patients. In rat periodontitis model, significant transcriptomic changes occurred across gingival regions, especially in the suprabasal epithelium, affecting autophagy and immune defense. Both bulk and spatial transcriptomic analyses indicate that JAK-STAT signaling was

documents.title: Integrative Genetic and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Macrophage-Associated Signatures and Predicted Macrophage-Fibroblast Communication in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
documents.abstract: How macrophage-associated expression changes relate to fibroblast extracellular matrix (ECM) programs in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the relationship between clinically associated macrophage expression patterns and fibroblast ECM programs and to examine their spatial correspondence.

documents.title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spat

documents.title: Identification of immune pathways regulating the cell mediated immunity in leishmaniasis in humans.
documents.abstract: A delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response induced by the intradermal inoculation of leishmanin antigen induced in individuals exposed to parasite Leishmania is a reliable indicator of cell mediated immunity (CMI). Leishmanin antigen skin test (LST) is also an important tool in disease surveillance studies in endemic area and can be used to assess vaccine efficacy. Previous studies assessing CMI in Leishmania exposed individuals were limited to analysis of PBMCs. To investigate the mediators of CMI, we performed spatial transcriptomic analysis of the DTH skin biopsies after leishmanin anti

documents.title: Beyond Genomic Alterations: Transcriptomic Profiling of Lineage Plasticity in Metastatic Solid Tumors.
documents.abstract: Lineage plasticity allows tumor cells to shift their differentiation state during metastatic progression and treatment. Genomic profiling identifies driver alterations and clonal relationships but does not fully characterize the lineage programs expressed by metastatic lesions. This review examines the complementary role of transcriptomic profiling and histopathology in assessing changes in tumor identity, with emphasis on colorectal, pancreatic, prostate, and lung cancers. We discuss studies of lineage transformation, intermediate cellular states, and loss of lineage fidelity, and their relat

documents.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
documents.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution ac

documents.title: Imaging Tumor Plasticity Across Space and Time: From Cell State to Metastatic Dissemination.
documents.abstract: Cancer cell plasticity-the capacity of tumor cells to alter phenotypic and functional states under microenvironmental and therapeutic pressure-contributes to invasion, metastasis, and therapy resistance, but is poorly captured by endpoint assays. This review asks which manifestations of plasticity current imaging and spatially resolved technologies can detect, and which conclusions their signals support. We critically reviewed studies using fluorescent and bioluminescent reporters, intravital microscopy, tissue clearing and light-sheet microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, multiplexed imaging,

documents.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
documents.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood.

documents.title: REV-ERBα/β Disruption Drives Environmental Tobacco Smoke-Induced Cellular Senescence Associated with cGAS-STING Signaling Promoting Lung Remodeling.
documents.abstract: Cellular senescence and DNA damage are recognized contributors to smoke-induced lung injury. However, how these processes integrate with circadian regulation and innate immune sensing in response to environmental stressors remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify a conserved multi-lineage transcriptional program in murine lungs that we define as the SCPS axis, characterized by Suppressed Clock, Primed Senescence (SCPS), fibrinolytic Shutdown, and cGAS-STING activation. We show that environmental cigarette/tobacco smoke (ETS) exposure induces senescence and SASP factor production in b

documents.title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
documents.abstract: Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD.

documents.title: A versatile set of computational tools for inference of genetic ancestry from human molecular data.
documents.abstract: Molecular properties of human diseases and conditions often exhibit dependence on the genetic ancestry of the donor. In order to make more human molecular data available for ancestry-informed research, we developed a set of software tools termed Robust Ancestry Inference using Data Synthesis (RAIDS) for inference of genetic ancestry from sequence data that pose challenges to genotyping. The data-synthesis procedure, underlying RAIDS, makes it a unique tool capable of assessing and optimizing the accuracy of inference for each individual molecular profile, with no resort to cohort data. Here we
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: FViT: A Foundation-Tokenized Vision Transformer with Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Scale Ensembling for Deep Learning-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology.
documents.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue morphology but is too costly for routine clinical use, motivating prediction of expression from hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) images. FViT (Foundation-tokenized Vision Transformer) tokenizes a spot and its k nearest neighbours with the frozen foundation model Phikon, fuses the tokens with a small trainable Transformer with a relative-position embedding, predicts expression directly and by k-nearest-neighbour retrieval of measured training expression, and combines three neighbourhood sizes (k = 8, 16, 24) in a weighted ensemble. We evaluated

documents.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. Although multiple computational methods have been developed to integrate bulk transcriptomic and single-cell data for phenotype-associated cell identification, differences in algorithmic strategies, parameter configurations, software implementations, and output formats make it difficult to compare methods fairly, reproduce analyses, and determine which approach is most suitable for a given bi

documents.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Dissection of Macrophage-Associated Inflammatory Signalling in Endometriosis-Associated Pain: A Hypothesis-Generating Study of Candidate Tissue-Level Genes.
documents.abstract: Background: Endometriosis is an oestrogen-dependent chronic inflammatory disease with chronic pelvic pain as a predominant and disabling symptom that severely compromises patient quality of life. The molecular mechanisms governing endometriosis-associated pain remain poorly elucidated. Given the lack of individual clinical pain scores in public datasets, this hypothesis-generating study aimed to characterise pain-correlated cell subsets and signalling programmes at single-cell resolution using a literature-based inflammatory gene module, and to identify replicable tissue-level candidate genes

documents.title: Deciphering Hepatic Host Transcriptomic Responses to Leishmania Infection: Integrating Evidence from In Vivo and In Vitro Studies.
documents.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a life-threatening, vector-borne systemic disease caused by the parasitic protozoans Leishmania donovani and Leishmania infantum. Among the affected organs, the liver represents a unique immunological environment in which, in commonly used experimental murine models, infection is often controlled through the coordinated formation of granulomas around infected Kupffer cells. However, effective hepatic parasite control does not necessarily result in complete parasite elimination, and the course of infection may vary across host species and experimental models. Unde

documents.title: SPACE-Tag Enables High-Throughput Spatial Chromatin Profiling With CUT&Tag.
documents.abstract: Spatial epigenomics maps chromatin states within intact tissues, yet current methods remain limited by accessibility and scale. We developed SPACE-Tag, a spatial CUT&Tag framework that converts epigenetic marks-associated DNA into polyadenylated RNA through T7-based linear amplification, enabling direct integration with standard spatial transcriptomic workflows. Applied to the mouse brain, SPACE-Tag resolved activating and repressive chromatin landscapes, recovered region-specific gene-regulatory programs across anatomical domains, and showed strong correlation with existing bulk and single-ce
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell perturbation data by optimizing causal reach of latent mediator dynamics.
documents.abstract: Resolving the causal structure of gene regulatory networks is central to understanding cellular regulation. Pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA readouts measure the transcriptional consequences of many interventions in parallel, providing a powerful resource for causal discovery. Combinatorial designs that perturb multiple regulators per cell increase throughput and can reveal responses that single-gene perturbations do not. However, inferring causal gene networks from these experiments remains challenging because gene regulatory interactions are nonlinear, dynamic, and often involve fe
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling.
documents.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulato
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Comparative molecular analysis of histopathologic subtypes reveals shared epithelial remodeling yet distinct fibroblast programs in scleroderma lung disease.
documents.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) drives mortality in systemic sclerosis (SSc), with a subset developing progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) resembling idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Despite recognition of two distinct histopathologic patterns, the cellular basis of nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) and usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) remains poorly understood.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: DiffKnock: diffusion-based knockoff inference for neural networks with applications to single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
documents.abstract: High-throughput single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies have revolutionized our ability to characterize cellular heterogeneity and dissect gene regulatory mechanisms. These data, however, are inherently high-dimensional and correlated, posing substantial challenges for statistical inference and feature selection. Identifying disease-related genes, while rigorously controlling false discoveries, remains a key challenge in scRNA-seq data analysis. Traditional methods often rely on parametric assumptions, which may fail to capture complex relationships and can suffer from inflated fal

documents.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre

documents.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d

documents.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
documents.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod

documents.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
documents.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

documents.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
documents.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.

documents.title: SWINGOT: Spatially Weighted Integration of Multi-Omics with Graph Optimal Transport.
documents.abstract: Background: Spatial multi-omics technologies help study tissue organization and spatial molecular patterns, but integration remains challenging. We aimed to integrate paired spatial multi-omics data while preserving relationships among spatial spots. Methods: We developed SWINGOT (Spatially Weighted Integration of Multi-Omics with Graph Optimal Transport), a topology-aware framework combining Wasserstein-based distribution alignment and Gromov-Wasserstein-based relational regularization. A conservative residual gated fusion strategy integrates modality-specific representations while limiting s

documents.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
documents.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient-and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
documents.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
documents.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n

documents.title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
documents.abstract: This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research.

documents.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics via the Scissor algorithm reveals APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages associated with osimertinib resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: The tumor microenvironment contributes to acquired resistance against osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the key cell subpopulations and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated.

documents.title: A ten-gene tyrosine-metabolism signature defines prognosis and reveals metabo-immune suppression in low-grade astrocytoma.
documents.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates dysregulated tyrosine metabolism in glioma malignancy; however, its cell-type specificity and clinical relevance in low-grade astrocytoma (LGA) remain undefined.

documents.title: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics identify a CD276-rich vascular matrix-associated CAF state linked to adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations have improved treatment outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but primary non-response and post-treatment residual progression remain common. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit marked heterogeneity and are closely associated with tumor treatment tolerance; however, specific stromal states associated with treatment non-response, post-treatment residual disease, and immune exclusion remain insufficiently characterized.

documents.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis supports a causal association of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with benign prostatic hyperplasia and interactions between VCAN-high fibroblasts and macrophages in hyperplastic prostate tissue.
documents.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are common among middle-aged and older men and can coexist clinically. However, the direction of causality and the underlying biological links between them remain unclear.

documents.title: Integrated bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses identify Crot-associated proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysregulation in murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
documents.abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) underlies acute kidney injury after transplantation, shock, and major surgery. Proximal-tubule metabolic dysfunction shapes injury and repair. Peroxisomes shorten fatty acids and export products, but their cross-omic behavior in acute renal IRI remains unclear.

documents.title: A deep-learning microglial response score integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for Alzheimer's disease stratification.
documents.abstract: Microglia exhibit diverse responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet linking these responses to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity remains challenging. We aimed to develop a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) integrating single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomics to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns.

documents.title: A metabolic state in the cancer-associated fibroblast differentiation continuum of colorectal cancer.
documents.abstract: The metabolic heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment remains poorly understood.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
documents.abstract: To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues.

documents.title: Clinical and single-cell integration identifies a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature in endometriosis.
documents.abstract: Stromal heterogeneity, regulated-cell-death-associated stress, and chronic inflammation contribute to endometriosis, but their relationships within specific stromal populations remain incompletely understood. This study integrated clinical characterization with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to investigate a TCF21-associated stromal death-inflammation signature.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Multi-omics characterization of fibroblast subpopulations involved in osteogenic differentiation in periodontitis.
documents.abstract: Fibroblasts are the predominant stromal cells in periodontal tissues and are involved in inflammation and repair. However, their heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Our study is to identify fibroblast subpopulations driving osteogenesis in periodontitis and their molecular markers.

documents.title: Multi-source analysis identifies an NPC2-associated macrophage transcriptional program in ulcerative colitis.
documents.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves extensive remodeling of intestinal macrophage states, but the molecular programs linking inflammation, lysosomal function, and lipid handling remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify macrophage-associated molecules and cellular states linked to UC.
